clue.text: Distinctive badge seen on outside of Danube carriage

indicators.note: the outside of the word Danube is its first and last letters only

parts.note: livery is a distinctive uniform or insignia worn by servants or a company's staff

explanation.surface: A distinctive emblem is painted on the side of a railway carriage travelling along the Danube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' here is the act of carrying goods, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage, in the sense of conveying goods to someone, is a synonym of the handing over of a parcel.

clue.text: A debt rescheduled to cover curious tattoo

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
a debt that is rescheduled has its terms rearranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for strange or curious

explanation.surface: A loan is restructured to pay for an odd tattoo on someone's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescheduled' rearranges A DEBT to D-BEAT, and 'to cover' puts RUM inside it. The 'tattoo' is the military drumming signal, not body art.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic drum signal, such as one sounded to call soldiers back to quarters.

clue.text: Idea essentially seen in computer network carrying a heavy burden

indicators.note: the central letters are placed within the network abbreviation

parts.note: LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: the essence of the word Idea is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: An idea runs through a computer network that is struggling under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden is an adjective for being loaded down or weighed with a heavy cargo.

clue.text: Reading of exchange with no deception

indicators.note: the swindle word is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: conversion is exchanging one currency for another
a con is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: An account of a currency exchange that was carried out honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading, as in an interpretation of a text or event, is one account or rendering of it.

clue.text: Charge to import last of grape harvest

indicators.note: importing brings the letter into the middle of the word

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

indicators.note: the last of grape is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tax is levied on bringing in the grape harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to gather in a crop, the verb sense of harvest.

clue.text: Puts on parties for men full of energy

indicators.note: the parties word holds the energy letter inside it

parts.note: stag parties are celebrations for a man about to marry
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone organises lively bachelor parties full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage and put on both mean to mount a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on before an audience; both are verbs of theatrical production.

clue.text: Article on church work results in dismissal

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the rest

parts.note: the is the definite article
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about church work leads to someone being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the chop is an informal idiom for being fired from a job.

clue.text: Beef stew given care

indicators.note: to stew is to cook ingredients together into a mixed dish, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A beef stew has been cooked with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like the stew's meat, but it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is informal slang for a complaint or grudge someone holds.

clue.text: Establishing a position, confess about sex appeal

indicators.note: the confessing word goes around the sex appeal word

parts.note: to sing is underworld slang for informing or confessing to the police
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: An informer admits to a seductive charm while staking out a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting something means choosing and fixing its location or placement.

clue.text: Type of service that's subject to writing?

definitions.meaning: an ... serve or delivery is made with the hand below the shoulder, as in tennis or bowling
read literally, something placed beneath the hand that writes, as paper lies under a writer's hand

explanation.definitionFit: Underhand describes a serve or throw delivered with the arm below shoulder level, and literally means beneath a hand.

clue.text: Doctor again designed procedure ultimately finding means of discharging liquid waste

indicators.note: the letters are planned out into a new arrangement
ultimately points to the very last letter of the word procedure

explanation.surface: A doctor once more devises a medical procedure to drain fluid from a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is a system of pipes or channels for carrying away sewage and surplus water.

clue.text: Be way out keeping score, losing heart

indicators.note: the way out holds the remaining letter inside it

parts.note: an exit is a way out of a building

indicators.note: the heart word is taken away from the word score

parts.note: core is the heart or centre of something

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly out of touch, clinging to a winning score yet losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' is the word core, not a middle letter: 'losing' strips it from score to leave one letter, and 'keeping' tucks that into the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be and to exist are synonyms for having reality or being alive.

clue.text: Criminal ring riots intermittently

parts.note: a band is a ring, as in a wedding band

indicators.note: taking letters intermittently means every other letter of the word riots

explanation.surface: A gang leader with a ring is sporadically causing riots.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw, a noun for a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Strain, and own New Jersey, for example

parts.note: to tax is to strain, as in taxing one's patience
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: It is a strain to own property in New Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Jersey' looks like the American state, but 'New' is only N; the definition is the Channel Island, known for low taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey, a self-governing island near France, is a well-known offshore low-tax jurisdiction.

clue.text: Suits worn by local for such a degree

indicators.note: the local word wears the suits word around it, so it goes inside

parts.note: fits means suits, as clothes that fit
near means local or close by

explanation.surface: Smart suits are worn by a nearby graduate for a degree ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine arts is the academic subject of painting and sculpture, awarded as a university degree such as a BFA.

clue.text: Length of focus given by new patent is not a name

indicators.note: making the words new means forming them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly granted patent is said not to cover a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PATENT IS NOT A to ATTENTIONSPA.
explanation.definitionFit: An attention span is how long someone can concentrate, so it is the duration of their focus.

clue.text: Exciting object found across stream

indicators.note: the object word spans across the stream word, holding it inside

parts.note: a thing is an object
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An exciting object has been discovered on the far side of a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling is an adjective for something that causes excitement and pleasure.

clue.text: Ecstasy used by the old man, bit of a looker?

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy
ye is an old form of the
a man in chess or draughts is a piece

explanation.surface: A drug is taken by an elderly man who fancies himself something of a good-looking type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of a looker' suggests an attractive person, but it is literally part of a viewing device.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyepiece is the lens you look through on a telescope or microscope, part of an instrument for looking.

clue.text: Short estimate written in log rarely reformed disreputable bunch

indicators.note: the shortened estimate is entered inside the rearranged letters
reformed means formed again in a new arrangement
short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a guess is an estimate

explanation.surface: A rough estimate in the logbook rarely reformed a disreputable bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' is the anagram signal for LOG RARELY, and 'written in' puts the clipped estimate into it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogues' gallery was a police collection of photos of known criminals, now any group of shady characters.

clue.text: Newcomer in India may be improvising, with tail all the way up

indicators.text: with tail all the way up
indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter travels from the bottom right to the top

parts.note: riffing is playing improvised musical phrases

explanation.surface: A new arrival in India might be making it up as they go along, all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Griffin was Anglo-Indian slang for a European newly arrived in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India a griffin was a recently arrived European, a greenhorn unused to local ways.

clue.text: Desire left, over booze and golf

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a lid on a box
gin is a type of alcoholic drink
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's desire has gone, after too much drink and golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing is a strong yearning or craving for something, a noun of wanting.

clue.text: One shows atmosphere exists over the legal profession

parts.note: is means exists
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: A tense mood hangs over the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atmosphere' suggests a mood, but it is the air pressure an isobar maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal air pressure.

clue.text: Makes joints, keeping one for military types

indicators.note: the joining word keeps the numeral inside it

parts.note: to solder is to join metal parts
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A metalworker makes joints, keeping one aside for some soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are members of an army, the kind of people one would call military types.

clue.text: Pitch from politician on spots rejected

indicators.note: in an across clue the politician comes after the spots
rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician's sales pitch is turned down because of a bad complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' is the verb of setting up a tent, not a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch camp, or pitch a tent, is to set up a camp, which is what encamp means.

clue.text: Excuse from party installed in first-class

indicators.note: the party word is put inside the first-class word

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written as AI in crosswords
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: An excuse from a party, put up in first-class accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse to avoid blame.

clue.text: Blackout sees regulars leaving for capital

indicators.note: the regular even letters leave, so only the odd letters of Blackout remain

explanation.surface: A power blackout means the regular customers leave for the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku is the capital city of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Silk knickers with the rear cut out?

indicators.note: the back end of the word, its last letter, is removed

parts.note: briefs are knickers or underpants

explanation.surface: A pair of silk knickers with an open back.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a senior barrister (a King's Counsel, who wears a silk gown), and a brief is barrister slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is a senior barrister, and brief is slang for a barrister or lawyer, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Steady head of industry lies about following attempt

indicators.note: the rest comes after the attempt word

parts.note: a stab is an attempt

indicators.note: the head of industry is its first letter
about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steady industry leader lies about trying something.
explanation.definitionFit: To steady something is to make it firm and unshaken, which is what stabilise means.

clue.text: Violent kid drinking spirit

indicators.note: the kid word swallows the spirit, holding it inside

parts.note: to kid is to tease, and so is to rag
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A violent child is downing spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging describes something wild and furious, such as a violent storm.

clue.text: Awkward situation of paper covering yearly meeting

indicators.note: the paper word wraps around the meeting abbreviation

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A newspaper's coverage of an annual meeting proves awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is literally a bog, and figuratively a tricky predicament that is hard to get out of.
